title: Compacted CSR KV Prefetch proto notes
content:
Purpose
-----
Notes for a small prototype to test a compact CSR-style layout for paged KV storage + a warp-aware prefetcher and tightly fused FlashAttention integration. Goal: reduce memory traffic and kernel launch overhead for long-context chat workloads while preserving end-to-end p99 latency.

Status
------
Draft exploratory notes. High-level plan for a week-long spike (microbenchmarks + simple synthetic harness). Not yet benchmarked on A100 vs H100. Rough perf expectations in the bottom.

Background and motivation
-------------------------
- Paged KV currently stores per-key/value blobs in fixed-size pages. Paging logic, eviction, and on-demand hydration work, but layout is wasteful for sparse slot usage (chat sessions with many short prompts).
- FlashAttention kernels perform best when token streams are contiguous and the kernel has predictable memory access patterns. Current paged-KV hydration causes many small indexed loads and extra pointer chasing.
- Multiple kernel launches per request (hydrate, decompress, copy-to-L2, run-attn) add launch overhead for low-token (<64) requests.

Idea summary
-----------
- Represent hydrated region(s) of KV as a compact CSR-like structure on device: two arrays (index_offsets, packed_kv_bytes). Each active token slot maps to a compacted entry (no per-slot padding).
- Maintain a small translation table (page->compact-offset + generation) to allow rollback when a page is evicted or partially updated. Use atomic updates to avoid races with inflight inference.
- Implement a warp-aware streaming prefetcher that:
  - scans a request's token indices and computes contiguous ranges in the compact buffer to prefetch into L2 (or register cache via cp.async where applicable)
  - emits a single fused kernel which performs prefetch + fused FlashAttention microkernel invocation on the compacted slice.
- Goal: fewer global loads, fewer kernel launches, higher effective bandwidth utilization for attention.

Data layout (compact CSR-ish)
----------------------------
- index_offsets: uint32[num_slots + 1] (offset in bytes into packed_kv_bytes)
- packed_kv_bytes: byte[] (variable-length contiguous concatenation of key,value vectors in serialized form)
- per-request token map: uint32[k] list of logical slot ids (these are translated to compact offsets via small page translation table)
- page_translation_table (per-device small table): struct { page_id -> base_compact_offset, generation, packed_size }
- On hydration, we append serialized kv to packed_kv_bytes and set index_offsets for corresponding logical slots. This is append-only until compaction step.

Why CSR-ish?
- Avoids fixed padding per slot; reduces device memory traffic when many slots are underutilized or lengths vary (sparse session activity).
- Enables contiguous reads for groups of tokens, improving coalescing in global loads.

Compaction and eviction model (sketch)
-------------------------------------
- Append-only until background compactor runs (hot compaction thread). Background compaction produces new packed buffer and updates translation_table atomically (swap pointer/generation). Inflight inference that references old generation is allowed; translation entry carries generation id.
- Eviction marks old pages as stale; compactor reclaims space and writes a new buffer. Simple: single-writer background compactor per-GPU to reduce concurrency complexity.
- Corner cases: concurrent writes to same logical slot -> must serialize at higher layer (request ordering / optimistic compare-and-swap on index_offsets).

Warp-aware prefetcher design
----------------------------
- Input: list of token slot ids for a batch of requests. Group by contiguous ranges in compact offset domain.
- For each group: schedule cp.async (if SM supports) to bring bytes into L2/register farm in aligned chunks (128B−1KB depending on SM).
- Heuristic: target chunk size ~= warp_size * vector_lane_bytes (e.g., 32 * 8 = 256B) + bank alignment. Evaluate 128B vs 256B on A100/H100.
- Prefetch ordering: prioritize ranges that will be used earliest in the attention sweep (recency-based).

Fused kernel plan
-----------------
- Kernel launch does: (1) prefetch chunks for a compact range, (2) decode/deserialize per-token keys/values into registers/shared memory, (3) run a micro-FlashAttention routine that consumes the registers directly (no intermediate writes to global), (4) write back results to output buffers.
- Micro-FlashAttention tweaks: expose an interface that accepts pointers into the compact buffer and lengths; internal loop does per-block unpack and softmax in shared memory using preloaded kv.
- For small heads/hidden sizes we'll run multiple warps per block; for large heads we allocate blocks to single head slices. Tune occupancy.

Launch and scheduling considerations
----------------------------------
- Kernel splitting: allow both single fused kernel for small requests and multi-stage pipeline for very large sequences to avoid SM starvation.
- Scheduler hints from runtime: mark requests with estimated compacted byte-size so scheduler can pack compatible requests into blocks (reduce tail). Use an int32 'compacted_bytes' in request metadata.
- Backpressure: if packed_kv_bytes read working set exceeds a threshold, fallback to current paged-kv path (safer) until compaction catches up.

Concurrency and correctness notes
--------------------------------
- Generation-based translation table: a request pins the generation id when it starts. If compactor swaps generation mid-request, request still uses pinned generation; compactor retains old buffer until grace period expires (refcount or epoch).
- Memory reclamation: background compactor maintains per-generation refcounts (incremented at request start, decremented at finish). Could piggyback epoch counters in kernel launch metadata.
- Atomicity for index_offsets updates: use compare-and-swap to set index_offsets from 0->offset; if concurrent, the winner wins and others read existing offset.

Fallback and compatibility
-------------------------
- Keep existing paged layout path unchanged. New code path is opt-in per-model or per-runtime flag.
- Fallback triggers: cp.async not supported, compaction backlog high, or unpack/deserialize errors.

Microbench plan and metrics
--------------------------
- Synthetic harness: generate workloads with 1) many short sessions (avg 8 tokens/session), 2) mix heavy sessions (256 tokens) + short ones, 3) worst-case random sparse slots.
- Measure: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, global memory bandwidth utilization, kernel launch counts per request, L2 hit rate (approx via perf counters).
- Targets: reduce per-request global loads by 30% for short-session workload; reduce kernel launches by 50% for common small-request path; no regression in p99 for long sessions > 128 tokens.

Initial micro-impl steps (week 1 spike)
--------------------------------------
1) Implement a simple host-side builder for compact buffer and index_offsets in Python/C++ in the harness (no compactor yet).
2) Implement a fused CUDA kernel prototype that accepts compact buffer + index_offsets and runs a minimal attention op (scaled dot-product + softmax) using prefetch via __ldg or cp.async if available.
3) Microbench against reference (current paged-kv + FlashAttention) with synthetic tokens. Collect launch counts, bandwidth, and tail latency.
4) If promising, add simple background compactor thread with generation swap.

Experiment notes and hypotheses
------------------------------
- Hypothesis A: compaction reduces uncoalesced reads significantly for chat workloads where only 10–30% of page slots are active. Expect 25–40% reduction in global memory reads.
- Hypothesis B: fused prefetch + FlashAttention reduces number of kernel launches and increases occupancy, improving p50 by 15–25% on small requests.
- Risks: compaction overhead may hurt throughput under heavy churn; complex correctness (concurrent writes) could add locking and negate benefits.

Open questions / TODOs
---------------------
- Should packed_kv_bytes be quantized/packed (int8) to further reduce traffic? That would complicate in-kernel unpack.
- Compactor GC strategy: simple LRU vs generational; which interacts better with session patterns we see in prod? Need metrics from usage traces (ask infra for sample trace).
- Which alignment/prefetch chunk size is best for H100's cp.async performance? Need microbench.
- Decide memory reclamation mechanism: epoch vs refcount. Epoch is simpler but requires tight clock.

Links and references
--------------------
- Internal PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serve-runtime/pull/912 (proto kernel)
- Related tickets: JIRA-RT-4872 (paged-KV perf), JIRA-RT-5001 (flashfusion API changes)
- Slack threads: #rt-kv-prefetch (see thread from Oct 2025)

Notes to self
------------
- Keep prototype simple: no partial-in-place updates to packed buffer at first. Append-only + compactor later.
- Instrument heavily: counters for bytes-prefetched, cp.async failures, generation-stale reads.
- Start with 16-bit head dims to test decode pipeline and then expand.

Appendix: rough pseudo-kernel sketch
-----------------------------------
// kernel(compact_buf, index_offsets, token_slots, out)
// 1. warp scans token_slots -> local list of compact ranges
// 2. for each compact range: cp.async to bring range into smem (aligned chunks)
// 3. deserialize kv entries into registers
// 4. run micro-attn using registers/shared memory
// 5. write results

(we'll prototype using __ldg first then try cp.async path)

End.
